news.headline: William and Kate meet PM Modi as they wrap up India tour
news.story_lead: - Published 18 November 2026, 13:01 GMT The Prince and Princess of Wales have met India's prime minister as they ended their three-day visit to the country. Narendra Modi thanked Prince William for bringing his Earthshot prize to the country during the couple's first international tour since 2022. It comes a day after the royal couple gave out Â£1m prizes to winners of the environmental award , which was founded by the prince and remains one of his biggest personal projects.
news.full_article_text: - Published 18 November 2026, 13:01 GMT The Prince and Princess of Wales have met India's prime minister as they ended their three-day visit to the country. Narendra Modi thanked Prince William for bringing his Earthshot prize to the country during the couple's first international tour since 2022. It comes a day after the royal couple gave out Â£1m prizes to winners of the environmental award , which was founded by the prince and remains one of his biggest personal projects. Catherine also visited a maternity hospital, where she comforted a grieving mother who lost a baby after giving birth to premature twin girls. - Street cricket with a legend then metro ride as William and Kate begin India visit Published 2 days ago On Wednesday, William and Catherine travelled from Mumbai to capital New Delhi for the final leg of their trip. During a meeting at Modi's private residence, a Kensington Palace spokesperson said the royals and Modi discussed the "strength and importance of the UKâIndia bilateral relationship, reflecting on the deep and enduring ties between the two countries and the opportunities to strengthen their partnership in the years ahead". The prince and princess also spoke "warmly" of their time in the country, thanking the prime minister and the people for their welcome, and saying how much they enjoyed returning to India, a decade after their last visit. Modi called it a "pleasure" to meet them, and said he looks forward to "further strengthening" the UKâIndia partnership for the "shared prosperity of the people of our nations and the wider world". When Prince William announced earlier this year that The Earthshot Prize ceremony was going to be held in India for the first time, he highlighted India's leadership in climate innovation, its biodiversity and its massive youth population as the key reasons for choosing the country. The royal spokesperson said that the meeting with Modi touched on the success of the ceremony in Mumbai, and India's "growing leadership in environmental innovation". The event, founded by Prince William in 2020, was hosted this year by Karan Johar, presenter of The Traitors India and one of the country's most well-known filmmakers. The couple last met the Indian prime minister on their official visit to India in 2016. Watch: Catherine visited a maternity hospital in Mumbai on the last day of royal visit Ahead of their meeting with Modi on Wednesday, William met with film stars during a visit to a film production company, while Catherine visited a maternity hospital, where she met grieving mother Jyoti Karande. As the future king and queen, they are viewed as a valuable diplomatic asset by the UK government. And with Catherine recovering well and back on international duties following her cancer treatment, visits of a similar kind can be expected to fill their calendar. news.headline: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
news.story_lead: Residents fled the area near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps following the Israeli evacuation order - Published 34 minutes ago Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents. Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes. The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.
news.full_article_text: Residents fled the area near Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps following the Israeli evacuation order - Published 34 minutes ago Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents. Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes. The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel. The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement. Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire. Early on Wednesday afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the incursion and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety. It also said a section of the north to south Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic. Later, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had begun a joint operation with the Shin Bet security service "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops". "IDF troops under the Southern Command are deployed in the area in accordance with the ceasefire agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat and thwart attempts by the Hamas terrorist organisation to harm Israeli civilians or IDF troops, or to violate the agreement," it added. Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement". Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the announcement. In one video verified by BBC Verify, a man can be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along Salah al-Din road, about 1.5km (0.9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he says. Automatic gunfire can be heard in another video filmed just to the south-east. A resident of Nuseirat who was forced to flee told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily programme: "The situation is now extremely dire, with Israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter." "We couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind." A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities". Asked about reported fatalities, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation. - Israel building new land barriers in Gaza and displacing families Published 30 July - Israel moves Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, satellite images show Published 16 January Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday. One man was killed in Nuseirat, the second to the north in Gaza City, and the third in the central town of Deir al-Balah, it added. The Israeli military said the first two strikes targeted "terrorists" and that it was not aware of the third incident, according to AFP news agency. At least 1,658 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since the ceasefire began last year, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. The Israeli military says six of its soldiers have been killed over the same period. Meanwhile, more than 1.9 million people - about 90% of Gaza's population - remain displaced, with 1.4 million of them living in tents or makeshift shelters, according to the UN. Reconstruction has yet to begin in Gaza, where an estimated 82% of all structures have been destroyed or damaged during the war, as US President Donald Trump's peace plan has largely stalled. The disarmament of Hamas has been a key sticking point. The group has agreed to give up its weapons in exchange for a phased withdrawal of Israeli troops from the 60% of Gaza they currently occupy. But Israel has insisted that Hamas must fully disarm before any pullout. The war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Since then, more than 74,700 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says. news.full_article_text: PM sets target for drug abuse eradication at council of ministers meeting Modi urged a concerted campaign against drug abuse, while highlighting poverty reduction and gains against left-wing extremism. Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday chaired a meeting of the council of ministers and underscored the need for a concerted campaign to eradicate drug use, said people aware of the details. According to a person privy to the meeting, the PM expressed concern over the widespread social evil and said drug addiction had emerged as a major challenge for the country. He said just as the government took stern measures against left-wing terrorism and managed to pull out millions from poverty, there was a need to act against drug abuse, this person added. “The prime minister was overcome with emotions when he spoke about the impact drugs use has on the younger demographic and said the social evil needs to be eradicated and no effort must be spared to do so...” said the person quoted above. The Union government has sharpened its campaign against drug abuse, particularly in poll-bound Punjab. In recent weeks, anti-drug campaigns have been the focus of Bharatiya Janata Party leaders including Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced that the party would fight the upcoming assembly elections in the northern state on the plank of “Nasha Mukt Punjab”(drug-free Punjab). On November 9, Shah at an event in Gujarat said that the Modi government now aims at creating a ‘Drug-free India’ by December 31, 2029. At the three-hour meeting held at Bharat Mandapam in the Capital, two presentations on poverty alleviation and LWE eradication and cyber security were also made. The poverty alleviation presentation was made by Anuradha Thakur, secretary, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA) and LWE eradication was discussed by Govind Mohan, Union home secretary. “The presentation on poverty alleviation measures highlighted how 500 million people have been pulled out of poverty and the economic progress made over the past 12 years,” said the person quoted above. The PM is learnt to have said that when the government was formed in 2014, he had referred to it as the government for the poor. He urged his colleagues to ensure that poverty alleviation measures were implemented well so that more people could have a quality life with access to health and education. Regarding the government’s achievements in curbing left-wing extremism, the PM cautioned that the government and law enforcement agencies must maintain their vigil to ensure that Maoism did not make a comeback. “The government set itself a target to eradicate Naxalism and has been successful in doing so. The PM said both achievements, of alleviating poverty and curbing LWE, need to be celebrated,” said the person quoted above. The ministers also discussed a World Bank poverty report stating that 500 million people were lifted out of poverty between 2011 and 2023, reducing the extreme poverty rate by 90%—from more than one in four Indians to roughly one in 38. The discussions also centered on governance reforms, employment generation, 100% saturation of welfare schemes, and targeted outreach toward youth and women—demographics heavily tied to India’s innovation and entrepreneurship push. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Smriti Kak Ramachandran Smriti covers an intersection of politics and governance. news.full_article_text: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on delay in finalising judges’ appointment procedure SC sought response of Centre, Secretary General of top court on petition seeking finalisation of amended MoP for appointment of judges to constitutional courts The Supreme Court on Wednesday sought the response of the Centre and the Secretary General of the top court on a petition seeking finalisation of an amended Memorandum of Procedure (MoP) for appointment of judges to the constitutional courts. The MoP is a set of documents governing the appointment, elevation and transfer of high court and Supreme Court judges. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale issued notice on a petition filed by Lok Prahari, an NGO, which questioned the delay in finalising the MoP despite a clear direction by a Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 2015 while striking down the National Judicial Appointments Commission and reviving the Collegium system for appointing judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts. Following the judgment which sought improved functioning of the Collegium system, an order was passed on December 16, 2025 for the Centre to finalise the existing MoP by supplementing it with the decisions taken by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant based on the unanimous view of the Collegium of the four senior-most judges of the top court. The petition also sought to bring the minutes of the selection process conducted by the Collegium of the Supreme Court and High Courts under the Right to Information (RTI) Act. The petition stated that since the issue relates to the appointment of judges, the matter deserves urgency because the dispensation of justice depends on the quality of judges appointed. The petition filed by advocate Shashank Singh said, “...the existing MoP suffers from the serious flaws of lack of transparency and objectivity affecting the quality, and thereby, the performance of the judges of the constitutional courts, directly affecting the litigants’ right to justice promised in the Preamble to the Constitution.” The petition named the Union of India and the CJI through the secretary general as respondents since the 2015 order required the CJI to take a decision on the MoP based on the unanimous view of the Collegium. “Ten years’ time was more than enough to comply with the decision of the Constitution Bench,” the petition said, adding, “Evidently, its implementation has been unduly delayed for no valid reason and it is a case of persistent breach of duty on the part of the respondent no. 1 (Centre) to comply with the order in this matter of great national and public importance relating to the top judiciary of the country.” The petition urged the court to issue a direction for finalising the MoP within a month and to ensure transparency and objectivity in the selection process by allowing the minutes of the meetings of the High Court and Supreme Court Collegiums for the selection of judges to be accessible to the public under the RTI Act.
